chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who performs an act of goodness, and a person sees him, and he is pleased by that. He said: 'There is no harm. There is no one who does not love that goodness be apparent for him among the people, provided that he did not do that for that [reason alone].'
ai.seo_question: Is it sinful to feel happy when people see your good deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between natural human vanity and the spiritual corruption of *riya'* (showing off), establishing that feeling pleased by public recognition is permissible provided the core intention (*niyyah*) remains sincere. This nuanced view, central to Shia jurisprudence of the heart, clarifies that the defect lies in making the audience the ultimate goal rather than a byproduct of the deed. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to monitor their inner states without falling into excessive self-scrutiny.
